newsitem.title: USA: South Africa's Tutu in U.S. for treatment.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Tutu in U.S. for treatment.

text.p: South African Archbishop Desmond Tutu is receiving treatment for prostate cancer in New York, a hospital spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The spokeswoman for the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Centre said the retired Anglican Archbishop of Cape Town was an outpatient at the hospital and she did not know how long he would be treated in the United States.
Tutu, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984 for his anti-apartheid efforts, had part of his prostate removed in January.

He said in March that the cancer appeared to be spreading and he would undergo three months of hormone treatment and radiation in South Africa and then receive radiation therapy in the United States for two months.

Tutu, 65, also said that while in New York he hoped to continue his work as chairman of South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which is hearing evidence of apartheid-era political crimes.
